title: DEX WebSocket reconnect: replaced providers are not destroyed, one reconnect loop per DEX races on ctx.wsProvider, no backfill, no heartbeat, and dashboard restart stacks a second close handler that later doubles every event

evidence.note: V3 reconnect: removeWsProvider, then a while(true) loop creating new WebSocketProvider (:1561), assigning ctx.wsProvider (:1562), re-subscribing, adding a close handler on the new socket (:1568)
removeWsProvider destroys only the provider cached in the map; providers created at bot.ts:1561/:1603 are never put in the map, so after the first reconnect nothing destroys the replaced provider
one close handler is added per DEX on the same raw socket: N DEXes on a chain = N independent reconnect loops, last writer wins ctx.wsProvider
onRestart calls startDexListener again for every DEX, which adds another close handler on the still-open socket
dashboard stop removes provider listeners but not the raw-socket close handlers
codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S2): DEX reconnects never backfill events missed during disconnection

sibling_sites_checked: V2 and V3 reconnect loops both checked (identical shape). provider.ts getWsProvider/removeWsProvider read. onRestart (:1808-1852) and the dashboard stop/start routes (chains.ts:121-190) read for listener stacking. No PairCreated/PoolCreated backfill exists anywhere in bot.ts (searched queryFilter: only the HTTP pollers use it). No ping/heartbeat in the DEX listener path. The anti-rug detector has its own reconnect (detector.ts ~918-926, ANTIRUG slice, RC-13); not edited here.
severity_rationale: Graded S1, above the research suggestion (S2, "S1 if it breaks anti-rug's consumer"). Reason: besides the S2 robustness defects (leaks, missed events, silent half-open socket), the code shows a path to a double buy: after a dashboard stop/start the raw socket carries two close handlers for one DEX; the next disconnect runs two reconnect loops, each subscribing the same listener on its own new provider, so every PairCreated reaches two concurrent handlers, which AUD-BUY-004 lets both buy. Status candidate until a Phase 23 run shows the duplicate dispatch. The anti-rug interaction (shared ctx.wsProvider) is RC-13, owned by the ANTIRUG slice.
recommendation: Fix together with RC-13 under card OD-11 (one per-chain WebSocket owner that notifies subscribers, destroys what it replaces, backfills the gap, detects half-open sockets and stops on shutdown); make listener registration idempotent so restart cannot stack handlers. Phase 24; nothing is changed in Phase 22.

triage.note: Reproduced on the real path with a real socket drop and fake time (plan 23-10, AC-12): the real listeners for every ETH DEX, then the real dashboard Stop and Start routes on the connected socket (the Start callback a source-pinned mirror of the private src/bot.ts onRestart); one server-side socket close then runs two reconnect loops per DEX within 10 s of fake time, each with its own disconnect alert and its own provider (claim restart-stacks-reconnect-loop); the control without a restart reconnects each DEX once. A startDexListener that registers its close handler once per DEX and socket reads looks fixed. Status candidate -> confirmed. The doubled PairCreated's double buy is AUD-BUY-004's test; the missing backfill, missing heartbeat and missing shutdown check stay code-read.
